A '''mausoleum''' was the final [[Burial/Legends|resting place]] of [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]],<ref name="Topps7">{{Topps|set=2012 Topps Star Wars Galaxy Series 7|cardname=Mourning for Padmé}}</ref> former [[Queen/Legends|Queen]] and then [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] of the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]], after her death in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]].<ref name="ROTS">{{Film|III}}</ref> Amidala's corpse, in spite of Naboo custom requiring cremation of the deceased,<ref name="SW:CL">[[Star Wars: Complete Locations (2005)|''Star Wars: Complete Locations'']]</ref> was contained within a rectangular sarcophagus decorated with the stylized [[Naboo royal crest/Legends|emblem of Naboo]], and a soft-[[Color/Legends|colored]] stained-glass [[Window/Legends|window]] showed the image of the deceased. On either side of the sarcophagus, a stone pot filled with [[Color/Legends|red]] [[Flower/Legends|flowers]] stood on a column. At some point after his transformation into the [[Armor/Legends|armored]] [[Darth/Legends|Darth]] Vader, Amidala's [[Marriage/Legends|husband]], the fallen [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] came to visit the mausoleum, stricken by grief and remorse for his part in her death.<ref name="Topps7" />

==Behind the scenes==
Padmé Amidala's mausoleum was first pictured on one of the trading cards from the ''[[2012 Topps Star Wars Galaxy Series 7]]'' set released by [[Topps]] in [[February]] [[2012]]. The card, titled "Mourning for Padmé," was illustrated by the [[Wikipedia:United States|American]] artist [[Erik Maell]].
